questions.explanation: Danışman bir sorunun raporda belirtilmesini ve sonuçların yorumunu etkileyebileceğini söyler; bu, yağmur nedeniyle bazı ölçümlerin bir hafta geç alındığını anlatan ‘Only one: heavy rain at two of the sites …’ yanıtını gerektirir. Raporun gelecek hafta yazılacağını (‘next week’) söylemek bir sorun bildirmez; alanların önceki ekipçe seçilmesi (‘previous team’) ve bulguları bir konferansta (‘conference’) sunma isteği yorumu etkileyecek bir sorun değildir; alanları hiç ziyaret etmemiş (‘never visited’) olmak ise veri toplama bilgisiyle çelişir.

Su ısıtıcısının en ucuzu (‘cheapest’) olması fişle ilgili değildir; elektronik eşyaları internetten (‘online’) alması ve ısıtıcıların yerini sorması (‘show me’) anlamsızdır; nakit iade (‘cash’) isteği ise görevlinin karttan söz etmesiyle uyuşmaz.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The experiment was so poorly designed that its results could not be used to draw any reliable conclusions.
options: Although the experiment was poorly designed, its results allowed researchers to draw reliable conclusions.
Because the experiment had been designed so badly, no reliable conclusions could be drawn from its results.
The results of the experiment were unreliable because the researchers drew their conclusions too quickly.
The experiment would have been better designed if its results had been more reliable.
Reliable conclusions can only be drawn from experiments that produce surprising results.
questions.explanation: ‘So … that’ yapısı neden-sonuç bildirir: Deney o kadar kötü tasarlanmıştı ki sonuçlarından güvenilir bir sonuç çıkarılamadı; ‘Because the experiment had been designed so badly …’ aynı ilişkiyi kurar. ‘Although … allowed researchers’ anlamı tersine çevirir; sorunu sonuçların ‘quickly’ çıkarılmasına bağlayan cümle nedeni değiştirir; ‘would have been better designed’ neden ile sonucun yerini değiştirir; ‘surprising results’ ise özgün cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Hardly had the scientists published their findings when other laboratories began trying to repeat the experiment.
options: The scientists published their findings only after other laboratories had repeated the experiment.
Hardly any laboratories tried to repeat the experiment after the findings were published.
Other laboratories started attempting to repeat the experiment almost immediately after the scientists published their findings.
Other laboratories found it hard to repeat the experiment because the findings were not published.
The scientists delayed publishing their findings until other laboratories had stopped repeating the experiment.
questions.explanation: ‘Hardly … when’ yapısı (… -er -mez) iki olayın hemen ardı ardına gerçekleştiğini anlatır; ‘almost immediately after’ aynı anlamı verir. Bulguların ancak deney tekrarlandıktan ‘only after’ sonra yayımlandığını söyleyen cümle sırayı tersine çevirir; ‘Hardly any laboratories’ yapıyı ‘neredeyse hiç’ anlamında yanlış yorumlar; bulguların ‘not published’ olduğunu ya da yayının ‘delayed’ edildiğini söyleyen cümleler de özgün anlamla çelişir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

It is not so much the cost of healthy food as the lack of time to prepare it that prevents many families from eating well.
options: Healthy food is so expensive that many families cannot afford to eat well.
Families who have more time to cook usually spend more money on healthy food.
Both the cost of healthy food and the lack of time prevent families from eating well to the same extent.
Many families fail to eat well mainly because they lack time to prepare healthy food rather than because such food is expensive.
Many families eat well because healthy food has become cheaper and quicker to prepare.
questions.explanation: ‘Not so much A as B’ yapısı asıl nedenin B olduğunu vurgular: Ailelerin iyi beslenememesinin temel nedeni maliyet değil hazırlık için zaman eksikliğidir; ‘mainly because they lack time … rather than because such food is expensive’ bunu aktarır. Nedeni yalnızca fiyata (‘afford’) bağlayan cümle vurguyu tersine çevirir; daha çok para harcama (‘spend’) ilişkisi cümlede yoktur; iki nedeni eşit (‘same extent’) sayan ve ailelerin iyi beslendiğini (‘cheaper’) söyleyen cümleler de anlamı değiştirir.

questions.passage: Bees are well known for their role in pollinating crops, but their health depends heavily on the variety of flowers available to them. ---- As a result, bee colonies in such landscapes may be weaker and more vulnerable to disease. Some farmers have therefore begun to plant strips of wildflowers along the edges of their fields.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Honey has been used as a sweetener and a medicine for thousands of years.
In areas dominated by a single crop, bees may find plenty of food for a few weeks but very little for the rest of the year.
Bees communicate the location of food sources through a series of movements known as a dance.
Consequently, wildflower strips have made farmland less attractive to bees.
Bumblebees are generally larger and hairier than honeybees.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki ‘As a result’ ve ‘such landscapes’ ifadeleri, öncesinde arıların besin kaynağının kısıtlı olduğu belirli bir arazi türünün anlatılmasını gerektirir; tek ürünün egemen olduğu alanları anlatan ‘In areas dominated by a single crop …’ bu bağı kurar. Balın tarihî kullanımı (‘Honey’) ve arıların dansla iletişimi (‘dance’) konudan sapar; çiçek şeritlerinin arazileri ‘less attractive’ yaptığı bilgisi son cümleyle çelişir; bombus arılarının bal arılarından iri olması (‘Bumblebees’) ise ‘such landscapes’ ifadesine dayanak oluşturmaz.

questions.passage: ---- In the eighteenth century, for example, ships on long voyages lost large numbers of sailors to scurvy, a disease that causes bleeding gums and extreme weakness. It was eventually discovered that the disease could be prevented by including citrus fruit in the sailors' diet. Today we know that scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C, a substance that the human body cannot produce itself.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Modern ships are equipped with refrigerators that allow fresh food to be stored for months.
Long before vitamins were identified, people noticed that certain diets could cause or prevent serious illness.
Vitamin C is also found in many vegetables, including peppers and broccoli.
Sailors in the eighteenth century were usually recruited from coastal towns.
However, citrus fruit was too expensive for most navies to buy.
questions.explanation: Paragraf ‘for example’ ile iskorbüt örneğine geçer; bu örneğin desteklediği genel bir giriş cümlesi gerekir: Vitaminler tanımlanmadan çok önce bazı beslenme biçimlerinin hastalığa yol açabildiği ya da önleyebildiği fark edilmişti; ‘Long before vitamins were identified …’ bu işlevi görür. Modern gemilerdeki buzdolapları (‘refrigerators’) ve C vitamininin sebzelerde (‘broccoli’) bulunması örnekle desteklenen bir genel fikir değildir; denizcilerin kıyı kasabalarından (‘recruited’) toplanması konudan sapar; ‘However’ ile başlayan cümle ise paragrafın başında anlamsızdır.

questions.passage: Many people assume that learning is most effective when information is studied repeatedly in a single long session. Research on memory, however, suggests otherwise. ---- This so-called spacing effect has been demonstrated in laboratories for more than a century, yet it is rarely applied in schools, where tests often encourage students to cram the night before.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Students who sleep well before an examination usually feel less anxious.
In many countries, the school year is divided into two or three terms.
Material that is reviewed several times with gaps of days or weeks between sessions tends to be remembered far longer.
Therefore, cramming the night before a test is the most efficient way to learn.
Some memory researchers have studied how ageing affects the ability to recognise faces.
questions.explanation: ‘Research … suggests otherwise’ cümlesinden sonra araştırmanın ne gösterdiği açıklanmalı, ardından gelen ‘This so-called spacing effect’ de bu bulguya gönderme yapmalıdır; aralıklı tekrarın daha kalıcı öğrenme sağladığını anlatan ‘Material that is reviewed several times with gaps …’ bu bağı kurar. Uyku ve kaygı (‘anxious’), okul döneminin bölümleri (‘terms’) ve yaşlanmanın yüz tanımaya etkisi (‘ageing’) aralıklama etkisini tanımlamaz; ‘Therefore, cramming … most efficient’ ise araştırmanın vardığı sonucun tam tersidir.

questions.passage: Volcanic eruptions can affect the climate far beyond the area where they occur. When a large eruption sends sulphur gases high into the atmosphere, these gases form tiny droplets that reflect part of the Sun's light back into space. ---- After the eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines in 1991, for instance, average global temperatures fell by around half a degree Celsius over the following year or so.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Volcanic soils are often very fertile and attract farmers.
Many volcanoes remain inactive for thousands of years before erupting again.
In contrast, such eruptions warm the planet rapidly for several decades.
Scientists have recently developed satellites that can track ash clouds.
As a result, the Earth's surface may cool slightly for a year or two.
questions.explanation: Güneş ışığının bir kısmının uzaya geri yansıtılmasının sonucu yüzeyin geçici olarak soğumasıdır; ardından gelen Pinatubo örneği de sıcaklıkların düştüğünü gösterir; ‘As a result, the Earth's surface may cool slightly’ bu bağı kurar. Volkanik toprakların verimliliği (‘fertile’) ve volkanların uzun süre etkisiz kalması (‘inactive’) iklim etkisinden sapar; ısınma (‘warm’) bildiren cümle örnekle çelişir; kül bulutlarını izleyen uydular (‘satellites’) ise yansıma ile sıcaklık düşüşü arasındaki bağı kurmaz.

questions.passage: (I) Before the twentieth century, letters in large cities were sorted entirely by hand, using only the street address written on the envelope. questions.explanation: Katılımcılar istenen davranışları abarttığı için öz bildirime dayanan bulgular ‘cautiously’ (temkinli biçimde) yorumlanmalıdır. ‘Abundantly’ (bolca), ‘permanently’ (kalıcı olarak), ‘voluntarily’ (gönüllü olarak) ve ‘fluently’ (akıcı biçimde) yorumlama eylemini bu gerekçeyle uyumlu biçimde nitelemez.

questions.text: The committee concluded that the available evidence was too ---- to justify any change in the national dietary guidelines, and it called for larger studies.
options: compulsory
hospitable
prosperous
fragmentary
vigorous
questions.explanation: Kurulun daha büyük çalışmalar istemesi, eldeki kanıtın değişikliği haklı çıkaramayacak kadar ‘fragmentary’ (parça parça, eksik) olduğunu gösterir. ‘Compulsory’ (zorunlu), ‘hospitable’ (konuksever), ‘prosperous’ (varlıklı) ve ‘vigorous’ (güçlü, dinç) kanıtın yetersizliğini anlatmaz; ‘vigorous’ üstelik ters bir anlam verir.

questions.text: Several coastal towns have had to ---- residents from low-lying neighbourhoods, as rising sea levels have made flooding far more frequent.
options: compensate
relocate
postulate
abolish
enrich
questions.explanation: Deniz seviyesi yükseldikçe sık su baskını yaşanan alçak mahallelerdeki sakinlerin başka yere ‘relocate’ (yerleştirmek, taşımak) edilmesi gerekir; ‘from’ edatı da bu fiille uyumludur. ‘Compensate’ (tazmin etmek) ‘from’ ile kullanılmaz; ‘postulate’ (varsaymak), ‘abolish’ (kaldırmak, yürürlükten kaldırmak) ve ‘enrich’ (zenginleştirmek) ise insanlarla bu bağlamda anlamsızdır.

questions.text: Rather than ---- on a single crop, many farmers in the region now grow a variety of plants in order to spread the risk of a poor harvest.
options: elaborate
dwell
comment
impose
rely
questions.explanation: Riski dağıtmak için çeşitli bitkiler yetiştirmenin karşıtı tek bir ürüne ‘rely’ (dayanmak, bel bağlamak) etmektir; ‘rely on’ kalıbı burada doğrudur. ‘Elaborate on’ (ayrıntılandırmak), ‘dwell on’ (üzerinde durmak, kafa yormak) ve ‘comment on’ (yorum yapmak) tarımsal bir tercihi anlatmaz; ‘impose on’ (dayatmak) ise nesnesiz kullanılamaz.

questions.text: Health officials hope that the new vaccination campaign will help ---- the outbreak before it reaches the neighbouring provinces.
options: give off
stamp out
put up with
look up to
take after
questions.explanation: Salgın komşu illere ulaşmadan önce aşı kampanyasıyla salgını ‘stamp out’ (bastırmak, kökünü kazımak) amaçlanır. ‘Give off’ (yaymak, salmak) koku ya da ısı için kullanılır; ‘put up with’ (katlanmak) amaçla çelişir; ‘look up to’ (saygı duymak) ve ‘take after’ (birine benzemek) ise kişilerle kullanılır.

questions.text: Hardly ---- the results been published when other laboratories began trying to replicate them.
options: have
did
had
was
has
questions.explanation: ‘Hardly … when’ kalıbı geçmişte art arda gelen iki olayı anlatır ve devrik ‘past perfect’ ister; ‘been published’ ile birlikte ‘had’ gelmelidir. ‘Have’ ve ‘has’ şimdiki zamanla bağlantı kurar ve ‘began’ ile uyuşmaz; ‘did’ ve ‘was’ ise ‘been’ ile yapı oluşturamaz.

questions.text: The drug, ---- side effects were initially thought to be mild, was withdrawn from the market after reports of serious liver damage.
options: whose
which
that
whom
where
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘side effects’ ilacın yan etkileridir; iyelik bildiren ilgi zamiri ‘whose’ gerekir. ‘Which’ ve ‘that’ ardından isim alarak iyelik anlatmaz (üstelik ‘that’ virgülle ayrılan cümlede kullanılmaz); ‘whom’ insanlar için nesne zamiridir; ‘where’ ise yer bildirir.

questions.text: If the dam ---- properly maintained, the flood would not have caused so much damage to the villages downstream.
options: has been
had been
is
would be
will be
questions.explanation: Ana cümledeki ‘would not have caused’ üçüncü tip koşul cümlesidir ve ‘if’ bölümünde ‘past perfect’ gerektirir: ‘had been’. ‘Has been’ ve ‘is’ gerçek bir durumu anlatır; ‘will be’ birinci tip koşula aittir; ‘would be’ ise ‘if’ cümleciğinde bu anlamda kullanılmaz.

questions.text: Participants were asked to avoid caffeine for at least twelve hours ---- the test so that their heart rates would not be affected.
options: in spite of
on behalf of
in terms of
apart from
prior to
questions.explanation: Kafeinden testten önceki on iki saat boyunca kaçınılması istendiği için ‘prior to’ (… -den önce) gerekir. ‘In spite of’ (-e rağmen) zıtlık, ‘on behalf of’ (adına) temsil, ‘in terms of’ (bakımından) ölçüt, ‘apart from’ (dışında) ise istisna bildirir; hiçbiri zaman ilişkisini kurmaz.

questions.text: Not until the early twentieth century ---- that certain diseases are caused by a lack of vitamins in the diet.
options: did scientists realise
scientists realised
scientists have realised
have scientists realised
scientists would realise
questions.explanation: Cümle başındaki ‘Not until’ olumsuz zaman ifadesi devrik yapı ister ve geçmişteki bir zamanı gösterdiği için ‘did scientists realise’ doğrudur. ‘Scientists realised’, ‘scientists have realised’ ve ‘scientists would realise’ devrik değildir; ‘have scientists realised’ devrik olsa da geçmişteki belirli bir zamanla ‘present perfect’ kullanılamaz.

questions.text: The more data a model is trained on, ---- its predictions tend to be, although this rule has clear limits.
options: more reliable
the most reliable
most reliably
the more reliable
the reliability
questions.explanation: ‘The more …, the more …’ (ne kadar … o kadar) karşılaştırma yapısının ikinci bölümü de ‘the + karşılaştırma’ ile kurulur: ‘the more reliable’. ‘More reliable’ başındaki ‘the’ eksik olduğu için yapıyı bozar; ‘the most reliable’ ve ‘most reliably’ en üstünlük ya da zarf biçimidir; ‘the reliability’ ise isimdir ve ‘tend to be’ ile uyuşmaz.

questions.text: The researchers would rather the findings ---- by independent experts before the policy was finalised, but the ministry went ahead anyway.
options: are reviewed
will be reviewed
had been reviewed
have been reviewed
be reviewing
questions.explanation: ‘Would rather + özne’ yapısı geçmişteki gerçekleşmemiş bir isteği anlatırken ‘past perfect’ ister; bakanlığın yine de ilerlemesi isteğin gerçekleşmediğini gösterir: ‘had been reviewed’. ‘Are reviewed’, ‘will be reviewed’ ve ‘have been reviewed’ gerçek zaman bildirir ve bu yapıda kullanılmaz; ‘be reviewing’ ise etken anlamlıdır ve bulgular kendileri inceleme yapamaz.

questions.text: ---- the treatment is highly effective, its high cost means that many patients in rural areas still cannot gain access to it.
options: Because
Unless
So that
Although
In case
questions.explanation: Tedavinin etkili olması ile hastaların ona ulaşamaması arasında zıtlık vardır; bunu ‘Although’ (-se de) kurar. ‘Because’ neden, ‘unless’ olumsuz koşul, ‘so that’ amaç, ‘in case’ (… ihtimaline karşı) önlem bildirir; hiçbiri bu zıtlığı anlatmaz.

questions.text: The bridge is thought ---- in the fourteenth century, although no written records of its construction have survived.
options: to build
to have been built
being built
to be building
having built
questions.explanation: Köprü kendisi inşa etmediği için edilgen, inşa geçmişte olduğu için de ‘perfect’ mastar gerekir: ‘is thought to have been built’. ‘To build’ ve ‘to be building’ etken anlamlıdır ve zamanı yanlış verir; ‘being built’ ve ‘having built’ ise ‘is thought’ yapısından sonra kullanılamaz.

questions.text: Many species of coral are so sensitive to changes in temperature ---- even a slight rise can cause them to expel the algae that feed them.
options: as
which
that
than
so
questions.explanation: ‘So + sıfat + that’ (o kadar … ki) yapısı sonuç bildirir; ‘so sensitive’ ifadesinden sonra ‘that’ gelir. ‘As’ ‘as … as’ karşılaştırmasında, ‘than’ üstünlük karşılaştırmasında kullanılır; ‘which’ ilgi zamiridir ve burada eksik öğe yoktur; ‘so’ ise yapıyı tekrar eder.

questions.passage: Statistics, in its modern sense, is a surprisingly young discipline. The word itself originally referred to the collection of information about the state, (1) ---- population figures, trade and taxation, which governments needed in order to raise armies and plan their revenue. In seventeenth-century London, the merchant John Graunt studied weekly lists of deaths and noticed that, (2) ---- individual deaths were unpredictable, the proportions dying of particular causes remained remarkably stable from year to year. His work is often regarded as the starting point of demography. In the nineteenth century, the Belgian astronomer Adolphe Quetelet went further, arguing that the regularities found in crime rates and body measurements revealed an 'average man' (3) ---- whom individuals could be compared. Such ideas were later (4) ---- by Francis Galton and Karl Pearson, who developed the concepts of correlation and regression, although their work was closely tied to eugenics, an association that historians now examine critically. It was only in the twentieth century, largely through Ronald Fisher's work on agricultural experiments, that statistics acquired the methods of randomisation and significance testing which, for better or worse, (5) ---- scientific research ever since.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: such as
in spite of
instead of
owing to
regardless of
questions.explanation: Nüfus sayıları, ticaret ve vergiler devlet hakkında toplanan bilgilere örnek olarak sıralanmıştır; örnek vermek için ‘such as’ (gibi) kullanılır. ‘In spite of’ (-e rağmen) zıtlık, ‘instead of’ (yerine) seçim, ‘owing to’ (nedeniyle) neden bildirir; ‘regardless of’ (-e bakmaksızın) da örnekleme ilişkisi kurmaz.

questions.explanation: Tek tek ölümlerin öngörülemez olması ile nedenlere göre oranların yıldan yıla sabit kalması arasında zıtlık vardır; bunu ‘although’ (-se de) kurar. ‘Because’ neden, ‘unless’ olumsuz koşul, ‘so that’ amaç bildirir; ‘once’ (-dikten sonra) ise anlamsız bir zaman ilişkisi kurar.

questions.explanation: ‘Compare against’ (… ile karşılaştırmak) kalıbında edat ilgi zamirinin önüne geçer: ‘an average man against whom individuals could be compared’. ‘Among’ (arasında), ‘beyond’ (ötesinde), ‘without’ (olmadan) ve ‘upon’ (üzerine) ‘compare’ fiiliyle bu anlamı vermez.

questions.passage: For much of the twentieth century, the standard response to coastal erosion was to build hard structures such as sea walls and groynes. These defences can protect the land directly behind them, but they frequently (1) ---- the problem elsewhere. A sea wall reflects wave energy (2) ---- absorbing it, which tends to scour away the beach in front of the wall, while groynes trap sand on one side and starve neighbouring beaches further along the coast. (3) ----, engineers have increasingly turned to so-called soft approaches. Beach nourishment, in which sand dredged from the seabed offshore is pumped onto eroding shores, is now common in the Netherlands and the United States. The Dutch 'Sand Motor', a vast artificial peninsula completed in 2011, was designed to let winds, waves and currents (4) ---- the sand gradually along the shoreline. Such schemes are not a permanent solution, (5) ----; the sand usually has to be replenished every few years, and the costs are likely to rise as sea levels continue to climb.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: confine
alleviate
diminish
settle
shift
questions.explanation: ‘But’ ile kurulan zıtlık ve sonraki cümledeki örnekler, sert yapıların sorunu çözmek yerine başka yere ‘shift’ (kaydırmak, aktarmak) ettiğini gösterir. ‘Alleviate’ (hafifletmek), ‘diminish’ (azaltmak) ve ‘settle’ (çözmek) zıtlığı ortadan kaldırır; ‘confine’ (sınırlamak) ise sorunu tek bir yerde tutmak anlamına gelir ve ‘elsewhere’ ile çelişir.

questions.text: Although enzymes are remarkably efficient catalysts, ----.
options: they are produced naturally by the cells of all living organisms
because they speed up chemical reactions without being consumed
industries therefore use them widely in detergents and food processing
the first enzyme was isolated from yeast in the nineteenth century
their activity can drop sharply outside a narrow range of temperature and acidity
questions.explanation: ‘Although’ zıtlık ister: Enzimler çok verimli olsa da etkinlikleri dar bir sıcaklık ve asitlik aralığının dışında hızla ‘drop’ edebilir (düşebilir). Bütün canlı hücrelerce ‘produced’ edilmeleri zıtlık değil olumlu bir ek bilgidir; ‘consumed’ ile biten seçenek ‘because’ yüzünden ana cümle kuramaz; ‘therefore’ zıtlığa ters bir sonuç bağlacıdır; ilk enzimin ‘yeast’ ile ilgili tarihçesi ise ilgisizdir.

questions.text: ----, the town council decided to restore the sand dunes rather than build a concrete sea wall.
options: Having learned that hard structures often worsen erosion on nearby beaches
Even though dunes had proved to offer no protection at all against storms
Unless residents agree to pay considerably higher local taxes
So that the beach would disappear more quickly
Because concrete sea walls had always proved cheaper and more effective
questions.explanation: Kumulları onarma kararının nedeni, sert yapıların yakın plajlarda erozyonu artırdığının ‘learned’ edilmesidir (öğrenilmesi). Kumulların fırtınalara karşı hiç koruma ‘offer’ etmediği bilgisi kararla çelişir; ‘taxes’ koşulu şimdiki zamanla kurulmuştur ve geçmişteki karara uymaz; plajın daha hızlı ‘disappear’ etmesi anlamsız bir amaçtır; beton duvarların hep daha ‘cheaper’ olduğu ise duvarı seçmek için bir gerekçe olurdu.

questions.text: The patients were monitored closely for several weeks after the trial ----.
options: whereas the drug had already been tested on thousands of healthy volunteers
as though they had never received the treatment at all
until the final report will be completed next year
so that any delayed side effects could be detected at an early stage
which most of them recovered from very quickly
questions.explanation: Hastaların haftalarca yakından izlenmesinin amacı, geç ortaya çıkan yan etkilerin erken ‘detected’ edilmesidir (saptanmasıdır); ‘so that’ amaç bildirir. ‘Whereas’ ile kurulan ‘volunteers’ seçeneği anlamsız bir karşıtlık kurar; ‘as though … never received’ izlemeyle çelişir; ‘until … will be completed’ dilbilgisi açısından yanlıştır (until ile gelecek zaman kullanılmaz); ‘which … recovered from’ ise ‘trial’ sözcüğüne mantıksız biçimde bağlanır.

questions.text: Had the authorities acted on the early warnings, ----.
options: the epidemic might have been contained within a single district
the number of new cases is now falling steadily
they will introduce stricter measures next year
the virus was first identified in a local hospital
hospitals have since become much better prepared
questions.explanation: ‘Had the authorities acted’ devrik üçüncü tip koşuldur ve ana cümlede ‘might/would have + V3’ ister: salgın tek bir bölgede ‘contained’ edilebilirdi (sınırlandırılabilirdi). ‘Falling’ ve ‘prepared’ içeren seçenekler gerçek şimdiki durumları anlatır; ‘will introduce’ gelecek zamandır; ‘identified’ içeren seçenek ise gerçek bir geçmiş olayı bildirir ve koşulun sonucu olamaz.

questions.text: ----, the students who studied worked examples performed better on the final test than those who had solved every problem on their own.
options: In order that the final test would be easier
Unless the problems had been far too difficult
Since nobody had taken part in the experiment
Contrary to what many of their teachers had expected
Although the worked examples were never shown to them
questions.explanation: Cümle öğretmenlerin beklentisine ters düşen bir sonucu sunar; ‘Contrary to what … expected’ (beklenenin aksine) buna uyar. Testin kolaylaşması ‘order’ amacı sonuçla ilgisizdir; ‘unless … had been’ koşulu geçmişteki gerçek sonuçla uyuşmaz; deneye kimsenin katılmaması (‘nobody’) sonuçla çelişir; örneklerin onlara ‘never’ gösterilmemesi ise örnek çalışan öğrenciler ifadesiyle çelişir.

questions.text: The money that migrants send home is often spent on schooling and health care, ----.
options: because most migrants find work in the construction sector
which suggests that it may bring long-term benefits to the receiving households
so that they rarely need to leave their home country
unless it had been sent through a mobile phone service
whose families had never received any financial support
questions.explanation: Paranın eğitim ve sağlığa harcanması, alıcı haneler için uzun vadeli yararlar sağlayabileceğini düşündürür; ‘which suggests’ önceki bilginin tamamına gönderme yapar. ‘Construction’ sektöründe çalışmak harcama biçimini açıklamaz; ‘rarely need to leave’ göçmenlerin zaten göç ettiği bilgisiyle çelişir; ‘mobile’ telefonla gönderilme koşulu hem zaman hem anlam bakımından uymaz; ‘whose’ ise önceki isme mantıklı biçimde bağlanamaz.

questions.text: No matter how carefully a sea wall is designed, ----.
options: engineers built the first ones along the coast in the nineteenth century
if it had been made of reinforced concrete
so that waves could no longer reach the town behind it
whether storms become more frequent in the coming decades
it cannot entirely prevent the gradual loss of sand from the beach in front of it
questions.explanation: ‘No matter how’ (ne kadar … olursa olsun) bir ana cümle ve ‘yine de’ anlamında bir sonuç ister: Duvar önündeki kumun yavaş yavaş kaybını tamamen ‘prevent’ edemez. ‘Nineteenth century’ ile ilgili tarih bilgisi bağlamla ilişkisizdir; ‘reinforced’ ile biten koşul cümleciği ve ‘whether’ ile başlayan yan cümle ana cümle kuramaz; ‘so that … could no longer’ ise yalnızca amaç bildirir ve zaman uyumu yoktur.

questions.text: Not only do antimicrobial peptides kill bacteria directly, ----.
options: while most antibiotics are produced by soil fungi
which is why they were first discovered in frog skin
but they also help to regulate the body's immune response
since they are too large to enter human cells
unless the infection has been caused by a virus
questions.explanation: ‘Not only … but also’ yapısı ekleme bildirir; peptitler bakterileri doğrudan öldürmekle kalmaz, bağışıklık yanıtını ‘regulate’ etmeye (düzenlemeye) de yardım eder. ‘Fungi’ ile ilgili karşılaştırma, ‘frog’ derisinde keşfedilme gerekçesi, ‘enter’ ile kurulan neden ve ‘virus’ koşulu yapının gerektirdiği ‘but also’ bölümünü sağlamaz.

questions.text: The census records were compiled so long ago ----.
options: than the historians had originally assumed
that it is now almost impossible to verify how the figures were collected
as if they had been gathered only yesterday
since statistical methods became more advanced
because nobody has ever consulted them
questions.explanation: ‘So + zarf + that’ (o kadar … ki) yapısı sonuç ister: Kayıtlar o kadar eski ki rakamların nasıl toplandığını ‘verify’ etmek (doğrulamak) neredeyse imkânsızdır. ‘Than’ ile başlayan seçenek karşılaştırma ister; ‘yesterday’ benzetmesi anlamsızdır; ‘advanced’ ile biten ‘since’ cümleciği ve ‘consulted’ içeren ‘because’ cümleciği ‘so’ yapısını tamamlamaz.

questions.text: ----, dengue is now spreading into regions that were once considered too cool for the mosquitoes that carry it.
options: Because the mosquitoes cannot survive in warm climates
Unless an effective vaccine had been developed
So that the virus would disappear from tropical cities
As average temperatures continue to rise
Whereas the number of reported cases has fallen to zero
questions.explanation: Hastalığın eskiden fazla serin sayılan bölgelere yayılmasının nedeni ortalama sıcaklıkların ‘rise’ etmesidir (yükselmesidir). Sivrisineklerin ‘warm’ iklimde yaşayamaması yayılmayı açıklamaz; ‘vaccine’ koşulu zaman ve anlam bakımından uymaz; virüsün ‘tropical’ kentlerden yok olması anlamsız bir amaçtır; vakaların sıfıra ‘fallen’ olması ise yayılmayla çelişir.

Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Although enzymes have been used in food production for thousands of years, it was only in the twentieth century that their chemical nature was understood.
options: Enzimlerin kimyasal yapısı anlaşıldıktan sonra binlerce yıl boyunca gıda üretiminde kullanılmıştır.
Yirminci yüzyılda enzimlerin gıda üretiminde kullanılmaya başlanmasıyla kimyasal yapıları da anlaşılmıştır.
Enzimler yirminci yüzyıldan beri gıda üretiminde kullanılmasına rağmen kimyasal yapıları hâlâ anlaşılamamıştır.
Enzimler binlerce yıldır gıda üretiminde kullanılsa da kimyasal yapıları ancak yirminci yüzyılda anlaşılmıştır.
Gıda üretiminde kullanılan enzimlerin kimyasal yapısı binlerce yıl önce keşfedilmiş olsa da yirminci yüzyılda yeniden incelenmiştir.

Para havaleleri yoksulluğu azaltmadığı için alıcı haneler bu parayı farklı biçimlerde harcamayı seçmektedir.
Para havalelerinin yoksulluğu ne ölçüde azalttığı, büyük ölçüde alıcı hanelerin bu parayı nasıl harcamayı seçtiğine bağlıdır.

Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Were coastal wetlands to disappear entirely, many inland areas would be exposed to far more severe flooding.
options: Kıyıdaki sulak alanlar tamamen ortadan kalktığı için iç kesimlerdeki birçok bölge şiddetli taşkınlara maruz kalmıştır.
İç kesimlerdeki taşkınlar şiddetlendikçe kıyıdaki sulak alanlar da hızla ortadan kalkmaktadır.
Kıyıdaki sulak alanlar tamamen ortadan kalkacak olsa, iç kesimlerdeki birçok bölge çok daha şiddetli taşkınlara maruz kalırdı.
Kıyıdaki sulak alanlar korunursa, iç kesimlerdeki bölgeler taşkınlardan tamamen kurtulacaktır.
Kıyıdaki sulak alanların bir kısmı yok olsa bile iç kesimler taşkınlardan pek etkilenmez.
questions.explanation: ‘Were … to disappear’ devrik ve gerçek dışı bir koşuldur (ortadan kalkacak olsa) ve ‘would be exposed to far more severe flooding’ (çok daha şiddetli taşkınlara maruz kalırdı) ile tamamlanır. ‘Kalktığı’ için diyen çeviri koşulu gerçekleşmiş bir olaya çevirir; ‘şiddetlendikçe’ neden ile sonucu tersine çevirir; ‘korunursa’ ve ‘kurtulacaktır’ farklı bir koşul ve kesinlik ekler; ‘etkilenmez’ ise anlamı tersine çevirir.

Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Bilişsel yük kuramına göre, öğrencilere aynı anda çok fazla yeni bilgi sunmak öğrenmeyi kolaylaştırmak yerine zorlaştırabilir.
options: Cognitive load theory claims that students learn more easily when they are given a large amount of information at once.
According to cognitive load theory, students should never be given new information until they have mastered the old.
Cognitive load theory was developed because students found it difficult to study several subjects at the same time.
According to cognitive load theory, presenting information slowly always makes learning more difficult for students.
According to cognitive load theory, presenting students with too much new information at once may make learning harder rather than easier.

Antimikrobiyal peptitlerin bakterilerde daha az direnç gelişimine yol açtığı düşünülse de bu varsayım son çalışmalarla sorgulanmaya başlanmıştır.
options: Although antimicrobial peptides are thought to cause less resistance in bacteria, this assumption has begun to be questioned by recent studies.
Recent studies have proved that bacteria can never develop resistance to antimicrobial peptides.
Because antimicrobial peptides cause more resistance than antibiotics, recent studies have stopped investigating them.
Antimicrobial peptides have been questioned in recent studies, so they are no longer believed to kill bacteria.
Recent studies assume that bacteria develop resistance to antimicrobial peptides more slowly than expected.

Direncin asla gelişmediğinin ‘proved’ edildiğini söyleyen çeviri anlamı tersine çevirir; araştırmaların ‘stopped’ edildiği bilgisi cümlede yoktur; peptitlerin artık bakteri öldürdüğüne inanılmadığını söyleyen ‘longer’ içeren çeviri varsayımın konusunu değiştirir; ‘slowly’ ile kurulan çeviri ise sorgulama fikrini kaybeder.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Dang hummasına karşı yaygın olarak kullanılabilecek etkili bir aşı henüz bulunmadığından, hastalıkla mücadele büyük ölçüde sivrisinek popülasyonlarının denetlenmesine dayanmaktadır.
options: Since there is not yet an effective vaccine that can be widely used against dengue, efforts to fight the disease rely largely on controlling mosquito populations.
Although an effective dengue vaccine has been developed, mosquito populations are still being controlled in many countries.
Controlling mosquito populations has made it unnecessary to develop a vaccine against dengue.

questions.passage: Enzymes, the protein catalysts that accelerate virtually every biochemical reaction in living organisms, have become indispensable to a wide range of industrial processes. They are employed, for instance, in the manufacture of detergents, the conversion of starch into sweeteners and the production of biofuels. The rational exploitation of these molecules, however, depends on a quantitative understanding of their behaviour, which is provided by the discipline known as enzyme kinetics. According to the model proposed by Leonor Michaelis and Maud Menten in 1913, the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction increases with the concentration of the substrate until the active sites of the available enzyme molecules become saturated. Beyond this point, the reaction proceeds at a maximum velocity that cannot be exceeded by the addition of further substrate. Two parameters derived from this model, the maximum velocity and the substrate concentration at which half of that velocity is attained, are routinely measured by industrial biochemists. These values allow the efficiency of competing enzymes to be compared and the dimensions of reactors to be estimated. Industrial conditions, however, rarely resemble those of the laboratory, where reactions are typically monitored in dilute solutions over relatively short periods. In large-scale reactors, the accumulation of products may inhibit the enzyme, elevated temperatures accelerate its gradual denaturation, and impurities in raw materials can bind to the active site and reduce catalytic activity. Consequently, kinetic parameters obtained under idealised conditions are regarded by many engineers as a useful starting point rather than as a reliable basis for predicting performance over weeks of continuous operation. To narrow this gap, researchers are increasingly combining kinetic measurements with computational models of entire processes and with enzymes modified through directed evolution to tolerate harsher conditions. It is hoped that this approach will reduce both production costs and the trial-and-error experimentation on which the industry has traditionally relied.
questions.text: The passage mainly focuses on ----.
options: the scientific rivalry between Leonor Michaelis and Maud Menten
the reasons why enzymes are no longer used in detergent manufacture
the value and the limitations of enzyme kinetics as a tool for industrial production
the chemical structure of the active sites of industrial enzymes
the environmental consequences of large-scale biofuel production
questions.explanation: Parça, enzim kinetiğinin endüstride neden yararlı olduğunu (enzimleri karşılaştırma, reaktör boyutunu tahmin etme) ve laboratuvar koşullarının endüstriyle örtüşmemesi yüzünden sınırlılıklarını anlatır. Michaelis ile Menten arasında bir ‘rivalry’ söz konusu değildir; enzimlerin deterjanlarda artık kullanılmadığı söylenmez, ‘detergent’ örneği yaygın kullanıma örnektir; aktif bölgelerin kimyasal ‘structure’ özelliği ve biyoyakıtın çevresel ‘environmental’ sonuçları ele alınmaz.

questions.text: According to the passage, once the active sites of the available enzyme molecules have become saturated, ----.
options: the enzyme is immediately destroyed by the heat of the reaction
adding more substrate no longer increases the rate of the reaction
the reaction comes to a complete stop
the concentration of the substrate must be reduced by half
the enzyme begins to produce different products

Enzimin hemen ‘destroyed’ edildiği söylenmez; tepkime durmaz, en yüksek hızda sürer, bu yüzden ‘complete stop’ yanlıştır; substratın yarıya ‘reduced’ edilmesi gerektiği ya da enzimin farklı ‘products’ üretmeye başladığı da belirtilmez.

already take into account the inhibiting effect of accumulated products

questions.passage: Antimicrobial peptides are short chains of amino acids produced by organisms as diverse as bacteria, insects, amphibians and humans. Constituting one of the most ancient components of innate immunity, they have attracted considerable attention as potential alternatives to conventional antibiotics. Unlike most antibiotics, which typically inhibit a single enzyme or metabolic pathway, many of these peptides carry a positive charge and are attracted to the negatively charged membranes of bacterial cells. There they insert themselves into the lipid layer and disrupt its integrity, causing the contents of the cell to leak out. Because such a mechanism targets a fundamental structural feature rather than a specific protein, it has frequently been argued that resistance would require extensive and costly modifications of the bacterial membrane and would therefore develop only rarely. This assumption has been challenged, however, by laboratory experiments in which bacterial populations exposed to gradually increasing concentrations of certain peptides acquired substantial resistance within a few hundred generations. Such findings have raised concern that the widespread therapeutic use of synthetic peptides might also weaken the natural peptides on which human immunity itself depends. Further obstacles to clinical application have been identified as well: many peptides are rapidly degraded by enzymes in the bloodstream, some exhibit toxicity towards human cells at high doses, and their large-scale production remains comparatively expensive. As a consequence, the small number of peptide-based drugs approved so far are administered mainly as topical preparations for skin and wound infections rather than as systemic treatments. Nevertheless, investigators remain cautiously optimistic, because chemical modifications designed to enhance stability and selectivity have yielded promising results in animal studies. Moreover, combinations of peptides with conventional antibiotics appear in some cases to restore the activity of drugs to which bacteria had previously become resistant.
questions.text: Which of the following could be the best title for the passage?
options: Antimicrobial Peptides: Promise and Obstacles
How Amphibians Survive Infections
The End of Bacterial Resistance
Why Antibiotics Target Single Enzymes
Producing Conventional Antibiotics Cheaply
questions.explanation: Parça antimikrobiyal peptitlerin antibiyotiklere alternatif olarak taşıdığı umudu, ardından direnç, yıkım, toksisite ve maliyet gibi engelleri ve temkinli iyimserliği anlatır; bu yüzden ‘Antimicrobial Peptides: Promise and Obstacles’ en uygun başlıktır. ‘How Amphibians Survive Infections’ yalnızca bir kaynak organizmaya odaklanır; ‘The End of Bacterial Resistance’ parçadaki direnç bulgularıyla çelişir; ‘Why Antibiotics Target Single Enzymes’ yalnızca karşılaştırma için geçen bir ayrıntıdır; ‘Producing Conventional Antibiotics Cheaply’ ise ele alınmaz.

questions.passage: Antimicrobial peptides are short chains of amino acids produced by organisms as diverse as bacteria, insects, amphibians and humans. Constituting one of the most ancient components of innate immunity, they have attracted considerable attention as potential alternatives to conventional antibiotics. Unlike most antibiotics, which typically inhibit a single enzyme or metabolic pathway, many of these peptides carry a positive charge and are attracted to the negatively charged membranes of bacterial cells. There they insert themselves into the lipid layer and disrupt its integrity, causing the contents of the cell to leak out. Because such a mechanism targets a fundamental structural feature rather than a specific protein, it has frequently been argued that resistance would require extensive and costly modifications of the bacterial membrane and would therefore develop only rarely. This assumption has been challenged, however, by laboratory experiments in which bacterial populations exposed to gradually increasing concentrations of certain peptides acquired substantial resistance within a few hundred generations. Such findings have raised concern that the widespread therapeutic use of synthetic peptides might also weaken the natural peptides on which human immunity itself depends. Further obstacles to clinical application have been identified as well: many peptides are rapidly degraded by enzymes in the bloodstream, some exhibit toxicity towards human cells at high doses, and their large-scale production remains comparatively expensive. As a consequence, the small number of peptide-based drugs approved so far are administered mainly as topical preparations for skin and wound infections rather than as systemic treatments. Nevertheless, investigators remain cautiously optimistic, because chemical modifications designed to enhance stability and selectivity have yielded promising results in animal studies. Moreover, combinations of peptides with conventional antibiotics appear in some cases to restore the activity of drugs to which bacteria had previously become resistant.
questions.text: According to the passage, many antimicrobial peptides kill bacteria by ----.
options: damaging the membrane that surrounds the bacterial cell
blocking a single enzyme involved in bacterial metabolism
attaching themselves to positively charged proteins
preventing bacterial cells from dividing
stimulating human cells to release antibiotics
questions.explanation: Parçada pozitif yüklü peptitlerin bakterilerin negatif yüklü zarlarına çekildiği, lipid katmanına girerek zarın bütünlüğünü bozduğu ve hücre içeriğinin dışarı sızdığı anlatılır. Tek bir enzimi ‘blocking’ etmek antibiyotiklerin yöntemidir; peptitler pozitif değil negatif yüklü zarlara çekildiği için ‘positively charged proteins’ yanlıştır; hücre bölünmesini ‘dividing’ engelleme ya da insan hücrelerini ‘stimulating’ etme parçada geçmez.

questions.passage: Remittances, the funds that migrants transfer to relatives in their countries of origin, have grown into one of the largest financial flows to low- and middle-income countries. According to World Bank estimates, they have in recent years exceeded the total volume of official development assistance to these countries. Early economic analyses tended to treat such transfers as private payments whose significance lay primarily in their contribution to household consumption and to national foreign-exchange reserves. Sociologists, by contrast, have emphasised that remittances are embedded in social relationships and are shaped by obligations, expectations and negotiations of status within transnational families. Ethnographic research has documented, for instance, that the regular sending of money is frequently interpreted by kin as evidence of continued loyalty. Migrants who fail to remit, conversely, may suffer a considerable loss of reputation in their home communities. Researchers have also drawn attention to so-called social remittances, a concept introduced by the sociologist Peggy Levitt in the late 1990s to describe the ideas, norms and practices that circulate between migrants and non-migrants alongside financial transfers. Attitudes towards gender roles, political participation and health care, it has been argued, may be gradually transformed through such exchanges, although the direction of change is by no means uniform. The consequences of remittances for inequality are similarly contested. Whereas some studies indicate that they alleviate poverty among recipient households, others suggest that the benefits are disproportionately concentrated among families that were relatively prosperous before any member emigrated, since migration itself requires initial resources. A growing number of scholars therefore argue that remittances should be analysed neither as a remedy for underdevelopment nor as a source of dependency, but as a complex social practice whose effects depend on the institutional context in which it takes place.
questions.text: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Remittances have replaced official aid as the main source of government revenue in poor countries.

Social remittances always lead to more progressive attitudes towards gender.

Havalelerin resmî yardımı aştığı söylenir ama hükümet geliri (‘revenue’) olduğu söylenmez; para gönderenlerin daha ‘poorer’ olduğu bilgisi yoktur; değişimin yönünün tek biçimli olmadığı söylendiğinden ‘always’ yanlıştır; havalelerin yoksulluğa ‘cure’ olduğu ise akademisyenlerin reddettiği bir görüştür.

questions.passage: Dengue, a viral infection transmitted chiefly by the mosquito Aedes aegypti, has been described by the World Health Organization as the most rapidly spreading mosquito-borne viral disease in the world. The number of reported cases is estimated to have risen roughly tenfold between 2000 and 2019. Although the majority of infections produce mild symptoms or none at all, a small proportion progress to severe dengue, a condition characterised by plasma leakage and bleeding that can prove fatal in the absence of appropriate hospital care. A distinctive feature of the disease is that four closely related types of the virus circulate, and infection with one type is thought to confer lasting immunity only against that particular type. Paradoxically, a second infection with a different type is associated with an elevated risk of severe illness. This phenomenon is generally attributed to antibodies from the first infection that facilitate, rather than prevent, the entry of the new virus into host cells. The mechanism has complicated vaccine development considerably, since a vaccine inducing an incomplete immune response might, in principle, behave like a first infection and thereby increase the risk of severe disease in some recipients. The epidemiology of dengue is further shaped by urbanisation, because Aedes aegypti breeds preferentially in small containers of stored water, discarded tyres and blocked gutters. Such breeding sites are abundant in densely populated cities that lack reliable water supplies and regular waste collection. Rising temperatures, moreover, shorten the time required for the virus to replicate inside the mosquito and are expected to extend the geographical range of the insect. Consequently, public health authorities increasingly emphasise community-based measures, such as the removal of standing water, alongside novel strategies including the release of mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia bacteria, which reduce the insects' capacity to transmit the virus.

options: is immune to all four types of the virus for the rest of his or her life
can no longer pass the virus to mosquitoes under any circumstances

will certainly develop severe dengue after any second infection
should never receive any kind of vaccine

Bağışıklık yalnızca tek tipe karşı olduğu için ‘all four types’ yanlıştır; virüsü sivrisineklere aktaramama (‘circumstances’) parçada geçmez; risk yalnızca artar, ‘certainly’ ile anlatılan kesinlik yoktur; aşı olunmaması gerektiği (‘never’) de söylenmez.

questions.passage: Why do some lessons leave students confused even when every step is explained clearly? According to cognitive load theory, developed by the Australian psychologist John Sweller in the 1980s, part of the answer lies in the limited capacity of working memory. Most people can actively process only a few new pieces of information at a time, whereas long-term memory can store a vast amount of knowledge in organised structures known as schemas. Learning, in this view, is the gradual construction of such schemas, and instruction succeeds when it helps learners build them without overloading working memory. Sweller and his colleagues distinguished between the load imposed by the inherent complexity of the material and the load created by poor instructional design, such as forcing students to switch their attention between a diagram and a separate block of text. One of the theory's best-known recommendations concerns worked examples. In a series of experiments, novices who studied fully solved problems before attempting similar ones on their own often learned more than those who were asked to solve problems from the start, presumably because searching for a solution consumed mental resources that could otherwise have been devoted to understanding. Interestingly, this advantage tends to disappear, and may even reverse, as learners become more expert, a finding known as the expertise reversal effect. Critics have pointed out that cognitive load is difficult to measure directly and that many studies have relied on students' own ratings of mental effort. Even so, the theory has had a considerable influence on teacher training, particularly in Britain and Australia, where its principles are now widely discussed.

Teacher Training Reforms in Britain
questions.explanation: Parça, çalışma belleğinin sınırlı kapasitesinden yola çıkarak öğretimin nasıl tasarlanması gerektiğini (bölünmüş dikkat, çözümlü örnekler) tartışır; bu yüzden ‘Working Memory and the Design of Instruction’ en uygun başlıktır. Sweller'ın hayatı (‘Career’) anlatılmaz; uzmanların daha hızlı unuttuğu (‘Forget’) söylenmez; zekâ ölçümü (‘Intelligence’) konu edilmez; Britanya'daki öğretmen eğitimi (‘Reforms’) yalnızca son cümlede kısaca anılır.

questions.passage: Why do some lessons leave students confused even when every step is explained clearly? According to cognitive load theory, developed by the Australian psychologist John Sweller in the 1980s, part of the answer lies in the limited capacity of working memory. Most people can actively process only a few new pieces of information at a time, whereas long-term memory can store a vast amount of knowledge in organised structures known as schemas. Learning, in this view, is the gradual construction of such schemas, and instruction succeeds when it helps learners build them without overloading working memory. Sweller and his colleagues distinguished between the load imposed by the inherent complexity of the material and the load created by poor instructional design, such as forcing students to switch their attention between a diagram and a separate block of text. One of the theory's best-known recommendations concerns worked examples. In a series of experiments, novices who studied fully solved problems before attempting similar ones on their own often learned more than those who were asked to solve problems from the start, presumably because searching for a solution consumed mental resources that could otherwise have been devoted to understanding. Interestingly, this advantage tends to disappear, and may even reverse, as learners become more expert, a finding known as the expertise reversal effect. Critics have pointed out that cognitive load is difficult to measure directly and that many studies have relied on students' own ratings of mental effort. Even so, the theory has had a considerable influence on teacher training, particularly in Britain and Australia, where its principles are now widely discussed.
questions.text: According to the passage, schemas are ----.
options: diagrams that teachers use to explain difficult material
small pieces of information processed in working memory
organised structures in which knowledge is stored in long-term memory
ratings that students give to their own mental effort
fully solved problems presented to beginners
questions.explanation: Parçada uzun süreli belleğin çok büyük miktarda bilgiyi şema denen düzenli yapılarda depoladığı açıkça söylenir. Öğretmenlerin kullandığı şekiller (‘diagrams’) şema değildir; çalışma belleğinde işlenen bilgi parçaları (‘pieces’) şemaların kendisi değil yapı taşlarıdır; öğrencilerin zihinsel çaba puanları (‘ratings’) ölçme yöntemidir; çözülmüş problemler (‘solved’) ise çözümlü örneklerdir.

questions.text: It can be inferred from the passage that, for learners who already have considerable expertise in a subject, ----.

worked examples remain the most effective method of instruction
cognitive load can easily be measured directly
diagrams and text should always be presented separately

questions.explanation: Parçada çözümlü örneklerin avantajının öğrenenler uzmanlaştıkça kaybolduğu, hatta tersine dönebildiği (uzmanlığın tersine dönme etkisi) belirtilir; buradan uzmanlar için bağımsız problem çözmenin daha yararlı olabileceği çıkarılır. Uzmanların çalışma belleğinin sınırsız olduğu (‘limits’) söylenmez; örneklerin en etkili yöntem olarak ‘remain’ ettiği bu etkiyle çelişir; yükün doğrudan ölçülmesinin zor olduğu söylendiğinden ‘easily’ yanlıştır; şekil ve metnin ayrı sunulması (‘separately’) ise kötü tasarım örneğidir.

questions.text: The author's attitude towards cognitive load theory can best be described as ----.
options: entirely dismissive of its practical value
openly hostile towards its main recommendations
completely indifferent to its findings
uncritically enthusiastic about all of its claims

questions.explanation: Yazar kuramın ilkelerini ve öğretmen eğitimindeki etkisini aktarırken eleştirmenlerin yükün doğrudan ölçülmesinin zor olduğu itirazını da belirtir; bu dengeli bir tutumdur. Etkisini vurguladığı için ‘dismissive’ ya da ‘hostile’ değildir; konuyu ayrıntılı biçimde ele aldığı için ‘indifferent’ de değildir; eleştirilere yer verdiği için ‘uncritically enthusiastic’ seçeneği de yanlıştır.

questions.passage:
Student: I read that some washing powders contain enzymes. Why would a detergent need them?
Chemist: ----
Student: So they work a bit like the enzymes in our stomach, only on clothes?
Chemist: That's a good way to put it, and they also let us wash at lower temperatures.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Most washing powders are sold in large supermarkets.
They break down stains made of proteins, fats and starch, much as digestive enzymes break down food.
Enzymes were first studied by chemists in the nineteenth century.
No, detergents never contain any biological ingredients.
You should always wash your clothes at the highest temperature.
questions.explanation: Öğrencinin enzimlerin midedeki enzimler gibi çalıştığı çıkarımı, kimyacının deterjan enzimlerinin protein, yağ ve nişasta lekelerini sindirim enzimlerinin besinleri parçaladığı gibi parçaladığını söylemesiyle anlam kazanır. Deterjanların ‘supermarkets’ içinde satılması, enzimlerin ‘nineteenth century’ içinde incelenmesi ve en yüksek sıcaklıkta (‘highest’) yıkama önerisi bu çıkarıma yol açmaz; deterjanlarda biyolojik içerik olmadığı (‘biological’) yanıtı ise öğrencinin sorusuyla çelişir.

questions.passage:
Engineer: The council wants to build a concrete sea wall to protect the promenade.
Ecologist: I understand why, but there's a risk they haven't considered.
Engineer: ----
Ecologist: The wall could reflect the waves and strip away the sand in front of it, so the beach itself might disappear.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: What exactly do you think could go wrong?
How long will it take to build the wall?
Who is going to pay for the construction?
Have you ever visited the promenade in winter?
Why don't we invite the council members to lunch?
questions.explanation: Ekolojist, düşünülmemiş bir risk olduğunu söyledikten sonra duvarın plajı nasıl yok edebileceğini açıklar; bu açıklama mühendisin tam olarak neyin ters gidebileceğini sormasına yanıttır. İnşaatın süresini soran ‘long’ sorusu, maliyeti kimin ödeyeceğini soran ‘construction’ sorusu, kışın gezinti yolunu ziyaret edip etmediğini soran ‘winter’ sorusu ve meclisi yemeğe davet etme önerisi (‘lunch’) ekolojistin yanıtıyla bağlantılı değildir.

questions.passage:
Teacher: My students seem overwhelmed whenever I introduce a new type of maths problem.
Colleague: ----
Teacher: You mean I should show them a few fully solved problems first?
Colleague: Exactly, and then gradually let them work on their own.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Maybe you should give them more difficult problems from the very start.
Maths has always been the least popular subject in our school.
Have you tried letting them study worked examples before they solve problems themselves?
I think the new textbooks will arrive next month.
Students usually concentrate better in the morning than in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: Öğretmenin önce birkaç tam çözülmüş problem göstermesi gerekip gerekmediğini sorması, meslektaşının çözümlü örnekler (worked examples) önerdiğini gösterir. Baştan daha zor (‘difficult’) problemler verme önerisi öğretmenin yanıtıyla çelişir; matematiğin en az sevilen ders (‘popular’) olması, yeni ders kitaplarının (‘textbooks’) gelişi ve öğrencilerin sabah (‘morning’) daha iyi odaklanması çözülmüş problemler fikrine yol açmaz.

questions.passage:
Journalist: Your study found that families receiving remittances spend more on schooling. Does that mean migration benefits everyone in the village?
Sociologist: ----
Journalist: So the poorest families may actually be left further behind?
Sociologist: In some communities, yes, that seems to be what is happening.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Yes, every family in the region now has at least one member working abroad.
Most migrants from the village work abroad for about five years.
Remittances are usually sent through banks or mobile phone apps.
Not necessarily. Migration is costly, so the households that can send someone abroad are often already better off.
Our study was funded by an international development organisation.
questions.explanation: Gazetecinin en yoksul ailelerin daha da geride kalabileceği çıkarımı, sosyoloğun göçün pahalı olduğunu ve birini yurt dışına gönderebilen hanelerin zaten daha varlıklı olduğunu söylemesine dayanır. Her ailenin yurt dışında bir üyesi olduğunu söyleyen ‘every family’ yanıtı bu çıkarımı desteklemez; göçmenlerin yaklaşık beş yıl (‘five years’) çalışması, paranın ‘banks’ ya da uygulamalarla gönderilmesi ve çalışmanın ‘funded’ edildiği kurum yoksul ailelerle ilgili bir sonuca yol açmaz.

questions.passage:
Patient: The doctor said I had dengue last year. Does that mean I'm immune now?
Nurse: ----
Patient: So a second infection could actually be worse than the first one?
Nurse: It can be, which is why avoiding mosquito bites is still important for you.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Yes, you can never be infected with dengue again.
Only partly. You're protected against the type you had, but another type could cause more serious illness.
Dengue is most common during the rainy season.
Your blood test results will be ready on Monday.
You should take antibiotics to prevent another infection.
questions.explanation: Hastanın ikinci bir enfeksiyonun daha kötü olabileceği çıkarımı, hemşirenin yalnızca geçirilen tipe karşı korunduğunu, başka bir tipin daha ağır hastalık yapabileceğini söylemesiyle anlam kazanır. Bir daha asla (‘never’) enfekte olamayacağı yanıtı bu çıkarımla çelişir; hastalığın yağmur mevsiminde (‘rainy season’) yaygın olması ve test sonuçlarının pazartesi (‘monday’) çıkacağı bilgisi ilgisizdir; antibiyotik (‘antibiotics’) önerisi ise viral bir hastalık için yanlıştır ve hastanın yanıtına yol açmaz.

questions.passage:
Student: Why is Ronald Fisher mentioned so often in my statistics textbook?
Lecturer: ----
Student: I had no idea that modern experimental methods came from farming research.
Lecturer: Few people do, but those field trials changed the way science is done.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: He was born in London in 1890 and later studied mathematics at Cambridge.
Because he wrote the textbook that you are reading now.
His ideas were completely forgotten soon after his death.
Because he was the first person ever to use the word "statistics".
Because he developed randomised experiments while studying crop yields at an agricultural research station.
questions.explanation: Öğrencinin modern deney yöntemlerinin tarım araştırmalarından çıktığına şaşırması, öğretim üyesinin Fisher'ın tarımsal bir araştırma istasyonunda ürün verimini incelerken rastgele deneyleri geliştirdiğini söylemesine dayanır. Doğum yeri ve ‘Cambridge’ eğitimi tarımla bağlantı kurmaz; ders kitabını ‘wrote’ ettiği söylenmez; fikirlerinin ‘forgotten’ olduğu iddiası sık anılmasıyla çelişir; sözcüğü ilk kullanan kişi olması (‘first person’) da tarımla ilgili bir çıkarıma yol açmaz.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Scarcely had the enzyme been added to the solution when the reaction began to accelerate.
options: The enzyme was added to the solution only after the reaction had begun to accelerate.
The reaction began to accelerate almost immediately after the enzyme was added to the solution.
Although the enzyme was added to the solution, the reaction did not accelerate.
The reaction accelerated gradually over several hours once the enzyme had been added.
Adding the enzyme to the solution slowed the reaction down unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: ‘Scarcely had … when …’ (… -er -mez) kalıbı iki olayın hemen ardı ardına gerçekleştiğini anlatır; doğru seçenek bunu ‘almost immediately after’ ile verir. ‘Only after’ olayların sırasını tersine çevirir; ‘did not accelerate’ hızlanmayı inkâr eder; ‘gradually over several hours’ anlıklık fikrini kaldırır; ‘slowed’ ise anlamı tamamen tersine çevirir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Unless instruction takes the limits of working memory into account, even lessons that are explained clearly may leave students confused.
options: Clearly explained lessons never confuse students, whatever the limits of their working memory.
Students are confused mainly because teachers explain lessons too slowly.
Even clearly explained lessons may confuse students if instruction ignores the limits of working memory.
The limits of working memory can be overcome if every lesson is explained more than once.
Teachers who understand working memory rarely need to explain their lessons.
questions.explanation: ‘Unless … takes into account’ (dikkate alınmazsa) koşulu, doğru seçenekteki ‘if instruction ignores’ (öğretim göz ardı ederse) ile aynı anlamı taşır; ‘even … may leave students confused’ da korunmuştur. ‘Never’ ve ‘whatever’ içeren cümle anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘slowly’ cümlede olmayan bir neden ekler; ‘overcome’ ve ‘once’ ile kurulan cümle farklı bir çözüm önerir; ‘rarely need’ ise anlatma gereğini ortadan kaldıran ilgisiz bir yargıdır.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Generous though remittances may be, they cannot on their own make up for the lack of public investment in rural areas.
options: Because remittances are so generous, rural areas no longer need any public investment.
Public investment in rural areas tends to decline whenever remittances become more generous.
Even if remittances are generous, they are not sufficient by themselves to compensate for inadequate public investment in rural areas.
Remittances would be far more generous if governments invested more in rural areas.
Rural areas now receive more money from remittances than from public investment.
questions.explanation: ‘Generous though … may be’ (ne kadar cömert olsa da) ve ‘cannot on their own make up for’ (tek başına telafi edemez) yapıları doğru seçenekte ‘even if … not sufficient by themselves to compensate for’ ile verilmiştir. ‘No longer need’ anlamı tersine çevirir; kamu yatırımının ‘decline’ ettiği ve hükümetler yatırım yaparsa havalelerin artacağı (‘would be far more’) bilgileri olmayan neden-sonuç ilişkileri kurar; ‘receive more money’ ise cümlede olmayan bir karşılaştırmadır.

questions.passage: Coastal engineers once assumed that beaches were fixed features of the landscape that could be held in place by concrete. ---- Sand is continually carried along the shore by waves and currents, and many beaches naturally retreat in winter and rebuild in summer. Modern coastal management therefore tries to work with these processes rather than against them.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Sea walls are usually built from concrete or large blocks of stone.
We now know, however, that beaches are highly dynamic systems.
Tourism is the most important industry in many coastal towns.
As a result, engineers stopped studying waves altogether.
Some beaches are covered with pebbles rather than sand.
questions.explanation: İlk cümle eski bir varsayımı aktarır, sonraki cümle ise kumun sürekli taşındığını anlatır; aradaki boşluğa bu varsayımı düzelten ‘highly dynamic systems’ cümlesi gelmelidir. Duvarların ‘stone’ ile yapıldığı bilgisi ve ‘tourism’ önemi akışı bozar; mühendislerin dalgaları incelemeyi bıraktığını (‘stopped’) söyleyen cümle sonraki açıklamayla çelişir; bazı plajların ‘pebbles’ ile kaplı olması ise kumun hareketiyle ilgili düşünceyi başlatmaz.

questions.passage: ---- During the Second World War, for instance, British officials used sample surveys to monitor what households were eating under rationing. In later decades, opinion polls and labour-force surveys adopted the same principle, showing that a carefully selected sample of a few thousand people could provide reliable information about an entire nation.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Rationing finally came to an end in Britain several years after the war.
Opinion polls are often criticised for influencing the way people vote.
Censuses that count every single person have now been abandoned in all countries.
The idea that a small, carefully chosen sample can represent a whole population gradually transformed the way governments gathered information.
Most people refuse to answer questions from survey interviewers.
questions.explanation: Paragrafın devamı, örneklem anketlerinin savaş döneminde ve sonrasında nasıl kullanıldığını örneklerle (‘for instance’) anlatır; bu nedenle boşluğa küçük bir örneklemin bütün nüfusu temsil edebileceği fikrini tanıtan konu cümlesi gelmelidir. Karne uygulamasının ne zaman bittiği (‘came to an end’) ayrıntıdır; anketlerin oy verme davranışını etkilediği eleştirisi (‘criticised’) konuyu değiştirir; nüfus sayımlarının her ülkede kaldırıldığı (‘abandoned’) iddiası doğru değildir; insanların çoğunun yanıt vermeyi reddettiği (‘refuse’) bilgisi ise anketlerin güvenilir olduğu sonucuyla çelişir.

questions.passage: Antimicrobial peptides are produced not only by humans but also by plants, insects and amphibians. The skin of many frogs, for example, releases a mixture of such peptides when the animal is injured or threatened. ---- This may help to explain why some frog species are able to live in muddy, bacteria-rich ponds without suffering frequent infections.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: These secretions can kill a wide range of microorganisms within a short time.
Frogs are found on every continent except Antarctica.
Many amphibian species are now threatened by habitat loss.
Some frogs can change the colour of their skin to match their surroundings.
Insects are by far the most numerous animals on Earth.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki cümle bazı kurbağaların bakteri dolu göletlerde neden sık enfeksiyon geçirmediğini açıklar; bu açıklama ancak deri salgılarının pek çok mikroorganizmayı kısa sürede öldürebildiği bilgisiyle anlam kazanır. Kurbağaların ‘Antarctica’ dışındaki her kıtada bulunması, ‘habitat’ kaybı tehdidi, renk değiştirme (‘colour’) yeteneği ve böceklerin sayıca en çok (‘numerous’) hayvanlar olması enfeksiyonlara karşı korunmayı açıklamaz.

questions.passage: In many tropical cities, dengue outbreaks follow a seasonal pattern, peaking during or shortly after the rainy season. Rainwater collects in flowerpots, buckets and old tyres, creating ideal breeding sites for mosquitoes. ---- Health campaigns therefore encourage residents to empty such containers at least once a week, especially during the wet months.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Dengue was first described in medical texts several centuries ago.
Most people infected with dengue do not develop any symptoms.
Some cities have built large dams to supply their residents with drinking water.
Because the insects can develop from eggs into adults in little more than a week, these small pools can quickly produce large numbers of mosquitoes.
Mosquitoes are attracted to the carbon dioxide that humans breathe out.
questions.explanation: Kampanyaların kapların haftada en az bir kez boşaltılmasını istemesi, sivrisineklerin yumurtadan erişkine bir haftadan biraz fazla bir sürede gelişebildiği bilgisine dayanır; haftalık boşaltma bu döngüyü kırar. Hastalığın tıbbi metinlerde ilk kez ‘centuries’ önce tanımlanması, çoğu enfeksiyonun ‘symptoms’ göstermemesi, kentlerin ‘dams’ inşa etmesi ve sivrisineklerin ‘carbon dioxide’ ile çekilmesi haftalık boşaltma önerisini açıklamaz.

questions.passage: (I) Since the 1960s, enzymes have been added to laundry detergents to remove stains that ordinary soaps struggle to dissolve. (II) Proteases break down protein-based stains such as blood and egg, while lipases attack fats and amylases digest starch. (III) Because these enzymes work efficiently at low temperatures, they allow clothes to be washed at 30 or 40 degrees, which saves a considerable amount of energy. (IV) Washing machines first became common in European households in the decades after the Second World War. (V) Manufacturers are now developing enzymes that remain stable for longer in liquid detergents, so that products can be stored without losing their effectiveness.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf deterjanlara eklenen enzimleri anlatır: kullanılmaya başlanmaları, hangi lekeleri parçaladıkları, düşük sıcaklıkta enerji tasarrufu sağlamaları ve sıvı deterjanlarda daha kararlı enzimler geliştirilmesi. IV numaralı cümle ise çamaşır makinelerinin Avrupa evlerinde yaygınlaşma tarihinden söz ederek enzimlerden uzaklaşır; I, II, III ve V enzimlerin deterjandaki rolünü işler.

questions.passage: (I) For centuries, cheesemakers curdled milk with rennet, an extract taken from the stomachs of young calves. (II) Its active ingredient is chymosin, an enzyme that cuts a specific milk protein and causes the milk to separate into solid curds and liquid whey. (III) Many hard cheeses are then left to ripen in cool cellars for months or even years, during which their flavour gradually becomes stronger. (IV) As demand for cheese grew during the twentieth century, however, the supply of calf rennet could no longer keep pace with production. (V) Since the early 1990s, much of the chymosin used in cheesemaking has therefore been produced by genetically modified microorganisms, which yield the same enzyme without the need for animal stomachs.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf peynir yapımında sütü pıhtılaştıran enzimi anlatır: buzağı midesinden elde edilen peynir mayası, etken maddesi kimozinin sütü pıhtı ve peynir altı suyuna ayırması, artan talebin bu kaynağı yetersiz bırakması ve bu yüzden enzimin mikroorganizmalarla üretilmesi. III numaralı cümle ise peynirin mahzenlerde olgunlaşıp lezzetinin güçlenmesinden söz ederek peynir konusunda kalsa da maya enziminden uzaklaşır; I, II, IV ve V aynı düşünce çizgisini izler.

questions.passage: (I) Florence Nightingale is best remembered as a nurse, but she was also a pioneer in the use of statistics to influence public policy. (II) During the Crimean War, she collected data showing that far more soldiers were dying from preventable diseases than from wounds received in battle. (III) To make her findings accessible to politicians, she presented them in a circular diagram that is now known as a polar area chart. (IV) She was named after the Italian city in which she was born while her wealthy parents were travelling abroad. (V) Her charts helped to persuade the government to improve sanitation in military hospitals.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV

more people therefore learned to read than ever before
literacy remained limited to a small minority of Europeans for at least another two centuries
because paper was easier to obtain than parchment
if the Church had not opposed the spread of printed texts

questions.text: The city council decided to plant thousands of trees along its busiest streets ----.

questions.text: No sooner had the government announced the new tax on sugary drinks ----.

questions.passage:
The rapid expansion of electric transport and grid-scale energy storage has intensified concern over the long-term availability of lithium, a relatively scarce element whose extraction is geographically concentrated in a small number of countries and is frequently associated with considerable environmental costs. In response, materials scientists have devoted growing attention to sodium-ion batteries, which operate on essentially the same principle as their lithium-based counterparts. In both cases, positively charged ions are shuttled between two electrodes through an electrolyte during charging and discharging. Sodium, however, is among the most abundant elements in the Earth's crust and can be obtained cheaply from seawater or common mineral deposits, a fact that has led many analysts to regard it as a promising basis for a more secure supply chain.
The substitution is not as straightforward as it might initially appear. Because the sodium ion is considerably larger and heavier than the lithium ion, its insertion into conventional electrode materials tends to cause structural strain, and the graphite anodes used in most lithium-ion cells are largely unsuitable for it. Researchers have consequently turned to alternative materials, notably so-called hard carbon, layered metal oxides and compounds resembling the pigment Prussian blue. A further limitation concerns energy density. Sodium-ion cells generally store less energy per kilogram than the best lithium-ion designs, which renders them less attractive for applications in which weight is critical.
Nevertheless, the technology offers compensating advantages, including better performance at low temperatures and a reduced risk of overheating, and several manufacturers have already begun commercial production. Most specialists therefore anticipate not the wholesale replacement of lithium but a division of labour, in which sodium-ion batteries are deployed primarily in stationary storage and low-cost vehicles, where price and safety matter more than compactness.

the history of rechargeable batteries since the invention of graphite anodes

Lityumun çevresel ‘damage’ı yalnızca giriş bilgisidir; pillerin ‘history’si, araçların ‘heavier’ hâle gelmesi ve yeni bir ‘method’ metinde ele alınmaz.

questions.passage:
Few areas of biomedicine have generated as much public expectation as stem cell research, owing to the capacity of certain cells to differentiate into a wide range of specialised tissues and thereby, in principle, to repair organs damaged by injury or degenerative disease. The translation of this potential into approved treatments, however, has proved considerably slower than early enthusiasts predicted. At present, only a limited number of stem cell-based therapies, most notably bone marrow transplantation for certain blood disorders, are regarded as established medical practice. For the majority of other conditions, the evidence of safety and efficacy remains at the stage of early clinical trials.
This gap between expectation and evidence has been exploited by a growing number of private clinics in several countries, which market unproven stem cell injections directly to patients for conditions ranging from arthritis to multiple sclerosis. Such interventions are frequently administered without the controlled trials that regulatory agencies normally require. Moreover, a number of serious adverse events, including infections, tumour formation and loss of vision, have been documented in the medical literature. Patients, many of whom suffer from conditions for which conventional medicine offers little hope, may pay substantial sums for procedures whose benefits have never been demonstrated.
Regulators have responded in divergent ways. Some agencies have tightened their oversight, insisting that products involving substantial manipulation of cells be evaluated as medicines, while others have introduced accelerated approval pathways intended to speed patient access to promising therapies. Critics of the latter approach contend that lowering the evidential threshold risks legitimising treatments before their effectiveness has been established, whereas its supporters maintain that excessively rigid rules may deprive seriously ill patients of their only realistic options.

Kemik iliği ‘transplants’ yalnızca bir örnektir; multipl sklerozun ‘cost’u ele alınmaz; hücrelerin doku oluşturamadığı (‘cannot’) iddiası metinle çelişir; klinik seçme ‘guide’ı da metnin amacı değildir.
